title: Fix logical property shorthands with calc(var()) not being converted (#927)
author: lukemartin
summary: Tailwind v4 emits `margin-block: calc(var(--spacing) * 0)` and `inset-inline: calc(...)`, which are kept as unparsed and never lowered to physical properties for old targets. The PR splits unparsed block/inline/inset shorthands into longhands when the value isn't a bare var(). Real user impact (Tailwind v4 + Chrome < 87 targets), but the single-value check looks too weak.
evidence: Master CLI (/home/user/lightningcss/target/review/ref-574eee2/lightningcss (master 574eee2)) `--targets 'chrome 84'`: `.foo{margin-block:calc(var(--s) * 0);inset-inline:calc(var(--s) * 2.5)}` unchanged (not lowered), confirming #927. Code-reading concern for review: `is_single_value` only excludes a token list that is exactly `[Var]`, so `margin-block: 10px var(--x)` or `inset: var(--a) var(--b)` would be copied whole into `margin-top`/`top` etc., producing invalid declarations (each must be one top-level component, not containing a bare var()/env() that could expand to several values). Duplicated logic across three arms. No maintainer comments.
